arguments.sql: SELECT (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM transactions t JOIN fraud_labels f ON f.transaction_id = CAST(t.id AS TEXT)) AS labelled_transactions, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM transactions) AS total_transactions, 1.0 * (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM transactions t JOIN fraud_labels f ON f.transaction_id = CAST(t.id AS TEXT)) / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM transactions) AS labelled_fraction
arguments.explanation: This counts the transactions that have a fraud label (marked either fraud or not fraud) and the total number of transactions. It also gives the labelled share as a fraction between 0 and 1.
assumptions: I took 'have a fraud label' to mean any label, whether it says fraud or not fraud. If you meant transactions marked as fraud, that is a different number.
I counted only labels that match a transaction, so the join with transactions decides what counts as labelled.
